result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources (test scope), whatever follows. The new tests and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass offline.

**Change**: in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, the two mock rules (lines 393–394) now use `[^/]*` instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`:
- `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
- `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

The old `mock` rule required at least one allowed character after `mock`, so a bare `mock/` folder was missed, and punctuation or non-ASCII characters broke the match. Because `[^/]*` stops at the next slash, the match stays within one folder name: `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/` and files like `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match. Backslash paths work because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries a slash-normalised form of the path.

**Tests**: I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It reads the private `testFilesConventions` list by reflection and checks the three new folder kinds, Windows paths, the previously classified folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`), and the non-matches. Both test classes pass (2 and 6 tests). I did not run the full module suite or a full `mvn install`.

I did not commit.
